issues.legal_issue: An amendment introducing a specific-performance claim is not allowable when it substitutes a new and inconsistent case based solely on a decree that conferred only a pre-emption right and is sought to avoid limitation.
material_facts: The original suit sought to enforce a pre-emption right created by a compromise decree.
During the appeal, the plaintiff sought to amend the plaint to allege an agreement of sale and claim specific performance.
The amendment relied on the same compromise decree; no separate agreement of sale was pleaded.
The original pre-emption claim faced a limitation bar.
issues.conclusion: The amendment was properly set aside because it introduced a new and inconsistent claim intended to overcome the limitation bar, and the compromise decree did not constitute an agreement for sale.
issues.legal_principle: An amendment that substitutes a new and inconsistent case and is sought to get around a limitation bar should not be allowed on these facts. A compromise decree providing that parties must sell allotted property among themselves confers a right of pre-emption but does not itself constitute an agreement for sale. No earlier case or statutory provision was relied on for this ruling.

rule.if: amendment_application_in_preemption_suit and decree_created_only_preemption_right and no_separate_sale_agreement_pleaded and amendment_sought_to_avoid_limitation

predicates.amendment_application_in_preemption_suit: A party to a suit seeking to enforce a pre-emption right applies to amend the pleading to claim specific performance.
predicates.decree_created_only_preemption_right: The decree relied on provided a right to buy property before it was sold to someone outside the specified group, without creating a sale agreement.
predicates.no_separate_sale_agreement_pleaded: The party seeking amendment does not plead a separate agreement of sale apart from the decree.
predicates.amendment_sought_to_avoid_limitation: The amendment is sought to avoid a limitation bar affecting the original claim.

issues.definition: When a party in a pre-emption suit relies only on a decree creating a pre-emption right, pleads no separate sale agreement, and seeks an amendment to avoid limitation, the amendment is not allowed.

issues.legal_issue: A suit to enforce a right of pre-emption is barred when it is brought more than one year after possession is delivered to the purchaser contrary to that right.
material_facts: The plaintiff sued to enforce a pre-emption right arising from a compromise decree.
The sale deed recited that possession was delivered to the purchaser on the date of sale, and the purchaser testified to delivery.
The plaintiff's own pleading also indicated that the property had been handed over after the sale.
The suit was filed more than one year after possession was delivered.
issues.conclusion: The pre-emption suit was barred by limitation because it was filed more than one year after possession was delivered to the purchaser.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 10 of the First Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1908, a suit to enforce a right of pre-emption must be brought within one year from the date the purchaser takes possession of the property contrary to that right.

predicates.preemption_suit: The proceeding is a suit to enforce a right of pre-emption.
predicates.possession_delivered_to_purchaser: The seller delivered possession of the property to the purchaser contrary to the claimed pre-emption right.
predicates.filing_after_applicable_one_year_limit: The suit was filed more than one year after possession was delivered to the purchaser.

issues.definition: A pre-emption suit is time-barred when the purchaser received possession contrary to the claimed right and the suit was filed more than one year later.

issues.legal_issue: A court may dismiss a suit as time-barred rather than continue a consent remand for trial when the limitation bar is established by the record, even if limitation was not initially pleaded.
material_facts: The appeal court had remanded the suit for a fresh trial by consent of the parties.
The original plaint, without the amendment, sought only enforcement of the pre-emption right.
The record established that possession had been delivered to the purchaser at the time of the sale and that the suit was filed more than one year later.
The limitation plea had not initially been raised in the written statement.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was right to dismiss the suit as time-barred instead of requiring further proceedings under the consent remand.
issues.legal_principle: A court must ensure that a suit barred by limitation is dismissed whether or not a party has raised limitation as a plea. Where the record sufficiently establishes the bar, the court need not prolong proceedings under a consent remand. The limitation rule applied was Article 10 of the First Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1908.

predicates.civil_suit: The proceeding is a civil suit.
predicates.consent_remand_for_trial: The parties consented to an order sending the suit for further trial.
predicates.limitation_bar_established_on_record: The record establishes the facts showing that the suit was filed outside the applicable limitation period.

issues.definition: When a civil suit has been remanded for trial by consent but the record establishes a limitation bar, the suit is dismissed without further trial.
